content.title: How Many Ties Have There Been in Oscars History?
content.text: Key PointsThe Oscars had a tie in Best Live Action Short Film at the 98th ceremony.Ties occur when nominees receive exactly equal votes; no tiebreaker is used, except for Best Picture.This was only the 7th tie in Oscars history, with prior ties listed across various categories. A tie has occurred for the 7th time in Oscars history! During the 98th Academy Awards on Sunday, Mar. 15, a rare tie occurred in the Best Live Action Short Film category between The Singers and Two People Exchanging Saliva. Ties only occur when nominees receive the exact same number of votes. The Academy does not have a tiebreaker system in place, however, the Academy and accounting firm PricewaterhouseCoopers told The Wrap that the Oscars would use tiebreakers to determine a single Best Picture winner if needed. What are the other ties in Oscars history? Best Actor: Fredric March (Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde) and Wallace Beery (The Champ) in 1932 Best Documentary Short: So Much for So Little and A Chance to Live in 1950 Best Actress: Katharine Hepburn (The Lion in Winter) and Barbra Streisand (Funny Girl) in 1969 Best Documentary Feature: Artie Shaw: Time Is All You’ve Got and Down and Out in America in 1987 Best Live-Action Short Film: Trevor and Franz Kafka’s It’s a Wonderful Life in 1995 Sound Editing: Zero Dark Thirty and Skyfall in 2013 🎬 SIGN UP for Parade’s Daily newsletter to get the latest pop culture news & celebrity interviews delivered right to your inbox 🎬 About the authorGrace Galante is a freelance journalist from Chicago with a passion for arts, culture, and entertainment stories.
